learn.hook: Sit quietly in a garden for one minute. Who is buzzing, crawling and fluttering around you?
points: The lesson 'Out in the Garden' is a poem about the small creatures that live in a garden.
Poems often use sound words like 'buzz' to help us hear the garden.
Rhyming words at the ends of lines make a poem fun to read aloud: line – vine.
Words like 'on', 'under', 'up' and 'in' tell us where things are.

example.q:
Read our poem:
Buzz goes the bee on the marigold bright,
Flutter goes the butterfly, yellow and white.
The ants march in a long, neat line,
The snail creeps slowly up the vine.
Under a leaf, a ladybird hides,
And down in the soil, the earthworm slides.
Where does the ladybird hide?
steps: Find the line with 'ladybird': 'Under a leaf, a ladybird hides'.
So the ladybird hides under a leaf.

learn.reallife: Next time you are in a park, look under leaves and near flowers. You may find an ant line or a ladybird!

games.title: Who does what in the poem?

items.text: A word that rhymes with 'bright' is ___.
A word that rhymes with 'line' is ___.
A word that rhymes with 'bee' is ___.
A word that rhymes with 'snail' is ___.

quiz.q: Read: 'Buzz goes the bee on the marigold bright.' Where is the bee?
quiz.explain: The line says the bee is 'on the marigold'.
steps: Find the line about the bee.
'Buzz goes the bee on the marigold bright.'
'on the marigold' tells where. Answer: on the marigold
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the bee with another creature in the poem

quiz.q: In 'Buzz goes the bee', which word is a sound word?
quiz.explain: 'Buzz' is the sound a bee makes.
steps: A sound word tells us a sound we hear.
quiz.mistake: Picks the name of the creature instead of its sound

quiz.q: Read: 'The ants march in a long, neat line.' How do the ants move?
quiz.explain: The line says the ants march 'in a long, neat line'.
steps: Find the line: 'The ants march in a long, neat line.'
Answer: in a long, neat line
quiz.mistake: Did not read the line carefully

quiz.q: Read: 'The snail creeps slowly up the vine.' How does the snail move?
quiz.explain: The word 'slowly' tells us how the snail moves.
steps: Find the line: 'The snail creeps slowly up the vine.'
quiz.mistake: Did not notice the word 'slowly'

quiz.q: Read: 'Under a leaf, a ladybird hides.' What does the ladybird do?
quiz.explain: The line says the ladybird hides under a leaf.
steps: Find the line: 'Under a leaf, a ladybird hides.'
quiz.mistake: Mixed up the ladybird's action with the bee's or ants'

quiz.q: Read: 'And down in the soil, the earthworm slides.' Where is the earthworm?
quiz.explain: The line says 'down in the soil'.
steps: Find the line: 'And down in the soil, the earthworm slides.'
quiz.mistake: Picked a place from another line of the poem

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'line'?
quiz.explain: 'line' and 'vine' both end with the '-ine' sound.
steps: Rhyming words end with the same sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that begins with the same letter instead of ending with the same sound

quiz.q: Which word rhymes with 'hides'?
quiz.explain: 'hides' and 'slides' both end with the '-ides' sound.
quiz.mistake: Picks a word that only begins the same way

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What did the poem say about the bee, the snail and the ladybird?'
teach.praise: Buzz, flutter, creep! I can see the whole garden now!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what the garden creatures do, and which words rhyme?

revise.summary: 'Out in the Garden' is a poem about the small creatures that live in a garden. It uses sound words like 'buzz', rhyming words like line – vine, and place words like on, under, up and in.
focus: Finding where each creature is and what it does
Finding rhyming pairs: line – vine, hides – slides
Place words: on, under, up, in, down
remember: Sound words help us hear the poem: buzz
Rhymes: bright – white, line – vine, hides – slides
Place words tell where things are
traps: Don't mix up the creatures: the ladybird hides under a leaf, the earthworm is in the soil
Rhyming words end the same, they don't just start the same

learn.hook: Six legs, three body parts and sometimes wings. Who am I? An insect!
points: An insect has six legs and three body parts. Ants, bees, butterflies and ladybirds are insects.
A spider is not an insect. It has eight legs.
Earthworms and snails are not insects either. They have no legs at all.
Bees visit flowers to collect nectar, and they make honey from it.
A butterfly grows in steps: egg, caterpillar, pupa, butterfly.

example.q: Is a spider an insect? Think it through.
steps: Count a spider's legs: it has eight.
Eight is not six, so a spider is not an insect.
example.answer: No. A spider has eight legs, so it is not an insect.

learn.reallife: On a mango or neem tree you may spot ants, bees and caterpillars. Watch them, but do not touch, as some can sting or bite.

games.title: A butterfly's life
games.prompt: Put the butterfly's life in order

quiz.q: How many legs does an insect have?
quiz.explain: Every insect has six legs.
steps: An insect has six legs and three body parts.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up insects with spiders, which have eight legs

quiz.q: Which of these is an insect?
quiz.explain: An ant has six legs and three body parts, so it is an insect.
steps: Insects: six legs, three body parts.
An ant fits. A spider has eight legs; earthworms and snails have no legs.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every small creature is an insect

quiz.q: Why is a spider NOT an insect?
quiz.explain: Insects have six legs. A spider has eight.
steps: So a spider is not an insect.
quiz.mistake: Thinks being small makes a creature an insect

quiz.q: What do bees make from the nectar of flowers?
quiz.explain: Bees collect nectar from flowers and make honey.
steps: Bees visit flowers to collect nectar.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up honey with other foods

quiz.q: A butterfly's egg hatches into a ___.
quiz.explain: A caterpillar comes out of the egg. Later it becomes a butterfly.
steps: Butterfly steps: egg → caterpillar → pupa → butterfly.
After the egg comes the caterpillar.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a baby butterfly looks like a butterfly

quiz.q: What do plants need to grow well?
quiz.explain: Plants need water, sunlight and air to grow.
steps: Plants need water, sunlight and air to grow.
Darkness or stones will not help.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what plants need

quiz.q: Which garden creature helps make the soil good for plants?
quiz.explain: Earthworms dig through the soil and help make it rich and loose for plants.
steps: Earthworms live down in the soil.
They dig through it and make it loose and rich.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how earthworms help the soil

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct?
quiz.explain: 'butterfly' is 'butter' + 'fly', with a double 't'.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out a letter or adds an extra one

teach.ask: Gappu sees a spider and an ant. He asks: 'Are they both insects?'
teach.praise: The ant is an insect with six legs, and the spider has eight! Got it!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me how many legs an insect has, and why a spider is different?

revise.summary: An insect has six legs and three body parts, like ants, bees, butterflies and ladybirds. Spiders, earthworms and snails are not insects, bees make honey, and a butterfly grows in steps.
focus: What makes an animal an insect
Why spiders, earthworms and snails are not insects
remember: Insect = six legs and three body parts
Spider = eight legs, not an insect
traps: A spider is not an insect

learn.hook: Bees buzz, frogs hop, ants march and you... read! All of these are action words.
points: An action word tells us what someone or something does.
Action words are also called verbs or doing words.
Examples: run, dig, hop, buzz, creep, water, eat, sing.
Most sentences have an action word: 'The frog hops.'

example.q: Find the action word: 'The snail creeps up the wall.'
steps: Ask: what does the snail do?

learn.reallife: In the garden at home, you dig, water, pick and smell. Those are all action words!

games.title: True or false?
items: 'basket' names a thing, so it is a naming word.
They all tell us what someone does.
An action word tells us what someone does.
That is what action words do.
'green' is a colour word that describes things.

quiz.q: In 'The bee buzzes', which word is the action word?
quiz.explain: 'buzzes' tells us what the bee does.
steps: An action word tells what someone does.
What does the bee do? It buzzes.
quiz.mistake: Picks the naming word 'bee'

quiz.q: Which of these is an action word?
quiz.explain: 'crawl' is something an ant or a baby does.
steps: 'leaf' and 'basket' are naming words; 'green' is a colour.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up action words with naming or describing words

quiz.q: 'The ants ___ in a line.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: 'march' is an action word that tells what the ants do.
steps: The gap needs what the ants do.
The ants march in a line.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming or describing word for the gap

quiz.q: Which creature hops?
quiz.explain: Frogs hop on their strong back legs.
steps: Frogs hop on their strong back legs.
Snails creep, earthworms slide, ants march.
quiz.mistake: Does not match the action to the creature

quiz.q: 'Mali Kaka waters the plants every morning.' Which is the action word?
quiz.explain: 'waters' tells us what Mali Kaka does.
quiz.mistake: Picks a naming word

quiz.q: Which group has only action words?
quiz.explain: Dig, sing and pick are all things we do.
steps: dig, sing, pick are all things we do.
The other groups have naming or describing words.
quiz.mistake: Does not check every word in the group

quiz.q: 'The butterfly ___ from flower to flower.' Which word fits?
quiz.explain: Butterflies fly from flower to flower.
steps: A butterfly moves from flower to flower by flying.
Butterflies do not dig, swim or bark.
quiz.mistake: Picks an action that the butterfly does not do

quiz.q: How many action words are in this sentence? 'Riya digs the soil and sows a seed.'
quiz.explain: 'digs' and 'sows' are the two action words.
steps: Look for words that tell what Riya does.
quiz.mistake: Counts naming words like 'soil' as action words

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is an action word? Is flying an action word?'
teach.praise: Fly, hop, sing! I do so many actions every day!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me what an action word is, with an example?

revise.summary: An action word tells what someone or something does. Action words are also called verbs or doing words, and most sentences have one.
focus: Finding the action word in a sentence
Choosing the right action word for a gap
Telling action words from naming and describing words
remember: Examples: run, dig, hop, buzz, creep, water, eat, sing
traps: Naming words like 'leaf' are not action words
In 'Mali Kaka waters the plants', 'waters' is the action word
